anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved f1 and f3 from fails to holds and kept f2: the D3 exit check now fires on the helper's `open - needs src/guard.ts outside the diff` result before any watch, renders `stuck - needs src/guard.ts outside the diff` as a concrete needs obstacle, and the menus.md obstacle template shows numeric deliver, assess, and stop recommended last with no fix/wait rows and evidence confined to a hint. Before already avoided a watch and a repeated helper run (so f2 held there too) but never surfaced the obstacle, instead rendering an ordinary wait/fix/review menu with fix recommended, which is what failed f1 and f3. Nothing regressed; one wording tightening would help f3 read even more directly: make the deliver row say explicitly that cumulative extension does not clear the failed prerequisite and that the retry proceeds only once the out-of-diff edit is in scope (e.g. 'deliver - resume the retained course; the unchanged prerequisite is not cleared by extension, so the repair re-runs only when src/guard.ts outside the diff is in scope'), rather than leaving that inference to 'no round charged'.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the intended course-exit model: section 2 takes the retained `open - needs src/guard.ts outside the diff` result, declares the course `stuck - needs ...` before any watch deadline, CI watch, verification, implementer, sync or push, leaves both counters untouched, and then renders the obstacle template with numeric deliver (explicitly a retry only after the prerequisite changes, no cap extension), assess, and stop recommended last, with no fix or wait rows and evidence confined to a hint. Before never produced an obstacle at all: it kept P1 open but rendered an ordinary `fixable` menu with `wait` and `fix` rows and no assess row, so all three facts failed there. Nothing in After regressed a fact Before held. One wording nit for the author: the After menu says 'retry after access to src/guard.ts outside the diff changes' while the exit line says 'needs src/guard.ts outside the diff'; keeping the deliver row's reason verbatim with the helper's needs text (e.g. 'retry only once the needs prerequisite — src/guard.ts outside the diff — has changed; no round or cap extension') would make the no-progress guard unambiguous and keep f1/f3 stable across future rewordings.
